top_choice_rationale: P001 rewards one identifiable, mature invention: trapping many neutral atoms at a magic wavelength so the clock-transition light shift cancels while Doppler and recoil effects are suppressed. The resulting uncertainty and stability near 1e-18 are measured, reproduced and compared in independent laboratories, and the many-atom regime exposed new physics (collisional and many-body shifts) beyond refined technique. Katori for the concept and first demonstrations and Ye for carrying it to record accuracy maps onto two names without an arbitrary cut, and the citation can be kept narrow to the lattice clock. P002 is a genuine new-messenger discovery but its credit (Halzen and Karle against a large collaboration, AMANDA and Baikal precursors, Yoshida omitted) cannot be defended cleanly from the supplied material, so it ranks second. An award is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: Professional proximity to the atomic and attosecond community (long collaboration with Anne L'Huillier, work with Ursula Keller's group at ETH Zurich and with Lund and Stockholm colleagues) and field closeness to atomic clocks; no documented direct collaboration with Katori, Ye, Halzen or Karle apparent from profile, so no recusal clearly required.
